original_question: For the same incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid model, do there exist time-periodic solutions without restrictions on the coefficients, external force, or initial data?
target_in_paper: Section 8 (On unsolved problems), second group of open problems for the incompressible Jeffreys/Oldroyd system (0.2), (0.4), (0.5), (2.18): the existence of time-periodic solutions, without restrictions on the coefficients, external force, or initial data.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the right model family (the incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid considered in the paper), the right qualitative object (time-periodic solutions), and the paper’s emphasis that the sought result should avoid additional restrictions on the coefficients, external force, and initial data.
missing_details: The paper’s open problem is attached specifically to problem (0.2), (0.4), (0.5), (2.18), not just to a generic 'Jeffreys-type model'.
The PDE system should be stated: div v = 0 and ∂_t v + (v·∇)v - Div σ + ∇p = f, with v the velocity, p the pressure, and σ the extra-stress tensor.
The boundary condition v|∂Ω = 0 (no-slip) is part of the model and should be included.
The constitutive law must be specified as σ + λ1 Dσ/Dt = 2η(E(v) + λ2 DE(v)/Dt), with E(v) = (∇v + (∇v)^T)/2.
The derivative D/Dt is not arbitrary: in Section 2 it is an objective derivative of the form d/dt + G(∇v,T) satisfying the objectivity condition (2.17).

The paper assumes the standard Jeffreys parameter relation λ1 > λ2 throughout this discussion; saying 'without restrictions on the coefficients' should therefore be read as 'without additional restrictive hypotheses such as smallness assumptions', not as removing the model-defining parameter regime altogether.
The ambient setting is a bounded domain Ω with boundary ∂Ω; Section 8 also notes that these issues are relevant for this model already in dimensions n ≥ 2.

The question belongs to the second group of open problems in Section 8, i.e. to problems specific to the Jeffreys/Oldroyd model rather than to the Navier–Stokes-type open problems listed just before it.
For the evolutionary problem, the paper explicitly says that one is asking for global-in-time solutions; this should be made explicit in a stand-alone formulation.
The paper does not broaden this item to uniqueness, stability, regularity, attractors, or inertial manifolds; adding those would go beyond the target statement.
refined_question: For the incompressible constant-density Jeffreys/Oldroyd model in a bounded domain Ω ⊂ R^n (with n ≥ 2), given by div v = 0, ∂_t v + (v·∇)v - Div σ + ∇p = f, the no-slip boundary condition v|∂Ω = 0, and the objective constitutive law σ + λ1 Dσ/Dt = 2η(E(v) + λ2 DE(v)/Dt), where E(v) = (∇v + (∇v)^T)/2 and D/Dt is an objective derivative in the sense of (2.17), does the associated evolutionary initial-boundary value problem admit global-in-time solutions that are periodic in time, without imposing any additional restrictive assumptions on the coefficients (beyond the standard Jeffreys regime λ1 > λ2), on the external force, or on the initial data?
justification: Section 8 isolates this as a distinct open problem in the second, model-specific group of unresolved questions for system (0.2), (0.4), (0.5), (2.18). The draft is close, but it leaves implicit the exact PDE system, the no-slip boundary condition, the role of the objective derivative, the standard parameter regime λ1 > λ2 assumed in the paper, the bounded-domain setting, and the fact that the evolutionary problem is being asked in the global-in-time sense. The paper does not state this item as a broader question about regularity, uniqueness, or attractors, so the refined version keeps the scope narrow and paper-faithful.
